meta.source: Coded from the published QP and mark scheme (J560/02, Wednesday 7 June 2023), downloaded from www.ocr.org.uk. Derived metadata only — question numbers, marks, mark-scheme codes and skill tags. No exam question text transcribed.
meta.note: J560/02 is one of OCR's two NON-calculator papers (the other is /05). 47 markers summing to exactly the printed 100, the only check OCR allows. Coded WITH mark_split, derived from OCR's part totals and partial-credit routes.

coding_notes: q7a and q7b tagged percentage_change, not growth_and_decay — the question states simple interest and the mark scheme's route for (b) is 700 + 3 × 14, a repeated addition rather than a multiplier.

q13a and q13bii are triangular-number pattern items. (a) is tagged sequences — the mark scheme's route is extending the term list and totalling. (bii) is tagged sequences too, with its distinctive step being recognising that consecutive triangular numbers sum to a square.
q18 tagged alternate_and_corresponding_angles then ratio: the parallel lines give x + y, and the 3 : 2 split turns that into x.
q20 tagged volume_of_a_prism then areas_of_triangles — the student's stated error is omitting the ½ from the triangular cross-section, which is what both marks turn on.

q21c (circle the child taller than expected) is the outlier-identification pattern flagged in OCR-JUN24-F-P2; tagged scatter_graphs here too, and the two move together if that 2026-09-04 ruling is ever extended.

q12a tagged systematic_listing: the mark scheme counts how many of the six orders are listed without repeats, which is the listing skill rather than a probability one. q12b is the probability read off that list.
